definitions.standard: The small, dense, positively charged center of an atom, containing protons and neutrons.
definitions.simple: The extremely tiny, heavy center of an atom where the protons and neutrons live.
definitions.scientific: The very dense region consisting of nucleons (protons and neutrons) at the center of an atom. It contains nearly all of the mass of the atom but occupies a minuscule fraction of its volume.

linguistics.origin: From Latin 'nucleus', meaning 'kernel, inner part', from nux 'nut'.

examples: The gold nucleus used in Rutherford's experiment

advanced_data.history: Discovered by Ernest Rutherford in 1911 through the gold foil experiment.

common_misconceptions: The nucleus is big compared to the atom. (No, if the atom was a huge football stadium, the nucleus would be a tiny pea in the center!).
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Point out the difference between an atomic nucleus (physics/chemistry) and a cell nucleus (biology).
